name_reason: Already fully compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: 'data_fd2_' prefix, 'chapter' domain, descriptor 'ch05_end_scene_char_pos_x_table' that reflects role and data type (per-chapter end-scene placement table/array). 'ch05' is a valid chapter domain ID (chapters 01-30), not a Ghidra address residue (table sits at 0x520cf, no hex-address suffix in name). Confirmed by reader fd2_chapter_05_end @ 0x231F9 which block-copies 7 bytes and passes them as the X-position arg to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro for the ch5 recruit cutscene (recruit char #10).
purpose: Chapter 5 end-scene character placement: per-character battle-tile X coordinate for the 7 chars staged in the chapter-5 recruit cutscene (recruit char #10).
logic_summary: First of three parallel 7-byte tables (X @ 0x520CF, Y @ 0x520D6, facing @ 0x520DD). Reader fd2_chapter_05_end @ 0x231F9 block-copies all 7 bytes (MOVSD/MOVSW/MOVSB) onto an on-stack scene-setup block, consumed one byte at a time (no struct stride, no wider element access, no sign extension), then passes the block as the X-position argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro @ 0x233C6.
element_semantics: Each entry is one character's battle-tile X coordinate (uint8, small tile coords 10..14). Values: {12, 11, 13, 10, 10, 14, 14}.
notes: Verified end-to-end: read_memory @ 0x520cf returns 0c0b0d0a0a0e0e (= {12,11,13,10,10,14,14}), matching the src declaration; the following 14 bytes are the adjacent Y (11,11,11,9,10,9,10) and facing (2,2,2,3,3,1,1) parallel tables, confirming the X/Y/facing @ 0x520CF/0x520D6/0x520DD layout. get_xrefs_to shows exactly one READ + one DATA fixup, both from fd2_chapter_05_end (single reader, zero writers => const). Decompile of fd2_chapter_05_end confirms element-by-element byte copy [0]..[6] and the call to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro; recruit char #10 confirmed by fd2_init_runtime_char_from_base_growth(10). Ghidra data plate was blank (null); created a concise plate (src is the authoritative content). Source comment block in chtab.c is already precise and accurate -> kept unchanged (no src edit, so only the shard is staged). run_script_inline initially failed on multi-line scripts using bare class names; fully-qualified single-statement form works (used to read plate=null and to write/read-back the plate).
